heading: Medical | Policies regarding Appointment Bookings
text: Policies regarding Appointment Bookings

heading: Medical | When patients make an appointment, they should use their own patient name and number. The appointment booked under your name would be your own appointment and cannot be transferred to other people.

heading: Medical | To protect the rights of individual patients, we will not entertain requests to cancel an appointment on behalf of someone else without the written authorization of the person with that booked appointment. Patients are encouraged to cancel their appointments themselves if necessary, using the online appointment booking system, by telephone, or in person.
text: To protect the rights of individual patients, we will not entertain requests to cancel an appointment on behalf of someone else without the written authorization of the person with that booked appointment. heading: Medical | To ensure fair access for all patients, any cancelled appointments will be made available to all eligible users on a first-come, first-served basis, whether through the online appointment booking system, telephone, or in person. As a general rule, we do not reserve empty slots for specific individuals.

heading: Medical Consultation for Children under the Age of 16
text: Medical Consultation for Children under the Age of 16

heading: Medical | It is desirable that all children under the age of 16 years attending the University Health Service are accompanied by a parent / legal guardian. It is because:
text: It is desirable that all children under the age of 16 years attending the University Health Service are accompanied by a parent / legal guardian. It is because:

heading: Medical | When children are ill, parental companionship and care are especially important for their recovery.
text: When children are ill, parental companionship and care are especially important for their recovery.

heading: Medical | Children feel more secure and are often more co-operative in the presence of a parent / legal guardian.
text: Children feel more secure and are often more co-operative in the presence of a parent / legal guardian.

heading: Medical | Certain procedures (e.g. injections, special tests, most dental procedures) require parental consent.
text: Certain procedures (e.g. injections, special tests, most dental procedures) require parental consent.

heading: Medical | Children cannot always describe symptoms accurately especially when it comes to duration or frequency.
text: Children cannot always describe symptoms accurately especially when it comes to duration or frequency.

heading: Medical | Children cannot always be relied upon to remember doctor’s verbal instructions.
text: Children cannot always be relied upon to remember doctor’s verbal instructions.

heading: Medical | A minor complaint may be the first signs of a more serious problem, which may require referral to specialist care or for hospitalisation.
text: A minor complaint may be the first signs of a more serious problem, which may require referral to specialist care or for hospitalisation.

heading: Medical | If the child cannot be accompanied by their parents / legal guardians, the child should at least be accompanied by a competent adult who holds full, delegated responsibility for the child. In such cases, a letter of authorisation signed by one of the parents / legal guardians is required.
text: If the child cannot be accompanied by their parents / legal guardians, the child should at least be accompanied by a competent adult who holds full, delegated responsibility for the child. In such cases, a letter of authorisation signed by one of the parents / legal guardians is required.
